questions.question: What is the primary function of a building foundation?
options: To improve the appearance of the building
To transfer structural loads safely to the supporting soil
To reduce the height of columns
questions.explanation: A foundation transfers loads from the structure to the ground while keeping soil pressure and settlement within acceptable limits.

questions.question: Which of the following is generally classified as a shallow foundation?
questions.explanation: An isolated footing is a common shallow foundation used to support an individual column.

questions.question: What does differential settlement mean?
options: Different parts of a structure settle by different amounts
questions.explanation: Differential settlement occurs when different foundation locations undergo unequal settlement, potentially causing cracks and structural distress.

questions.question: Which investigation is commonly used to assess subsurface soil conditions before foundation design?
questions.explanation: A geotechnical investigation helps determine soil layers, groundwater conditions and engineering properties relevant to foundation design.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents the usual load path in a conventional framed building?
questions.explanation: In a conventional framed structure, loads travel through slabs and beams to columns, then through foundations into the supporting ground. Some structures have different load paths.
